steps.title: An agent can propose, not spend
steps.body: OS is a self-hosted workspace for proposing payments and trades. The control plane coordinates requests. The signer decides whether it can sign. This tour describes the public source at c87c59c, not a live workspace. Select a component to read its notes.

steps.title: Review on the confirmation origin
steps.body: The first page is the control-plane inbox. It sends the person to the separate confirmation origin to read what the signer holds and approve with a passkey. The server’s policy check is early feedback, not the authority to sign.

steps.title: Approval is not a receipt
steps.body: A durable workflow collects the signer’s decision. The signer checks the exact intent and its own wallet limits before signing. The control plane then broadcasts the signed transaction and waits for a receipt. A pending or approved request has not necessarily landed.

steps.title: Approve a bounded series of transfers
steps.body: A mandate is advance approval for a narrow series of transfers. The signer keeps the grant and counts each use. An uncovered transfer returns to the normal inbox flow. A mandate does not authorize a venue order or withdrawal.

steps.title: Follow a limit order to the venue
steps.body: A venue order uses the same confirmation boundary as a payment, but the signer builds a venue action. The control plane submits it to Hyperliquid and follows its status. The repository documents tests against fake venues. It does not claim a real venue run.

steps.title: Keep coordination separate from authority
steps.body: The workflow continues after the person leaves the browser. Postgres stores workflow and control-plane state. The signer’s own records, not the copies shown by the web app, decide whether the approved operation can be signed.

steps.title: Choose how to isolate the signer
steps.body: Start with the documented Compose dev profile and test funds. The split-host layout puts the signer and confirmation service on their own host. These are deployment patterns in the repo, not a map of a live environment.

steps.title: Find the code behind each boundary
steps.body: Open the source link for the pinned repository snapshot. Start with docs/architecture.md and docs/approval-protocol.md, then use these component notes to find the code. The README distinguishes tested behavior from what is still unproven.

steps.title: Try the dev stack, not a real wallet
steps.body: If you want to try OS after this tour, follow the repository quickstart with test funds. This walkthrough is read-only. It does not run OS, connect to a wallet, or place orders.

items.name: Agent
items.description: Any MCP client can read allowed data, propose operations, and cancel its own requests. It does not hold wallet keys.

items.name: Person
items.description: A person manages a workspace and reviews requests in the web app. To approve, they follow the link to a different origin.

items.name: OS server
items.description: apps/server serves the control-plane API and MCP. It coordinates requests and execution, but it cannot authorize signing by itself.

items.name: Confirmation page
items.description: apps/approve serves the separate origin and relays the confirmation exchange to the signer. It does not hold wallet keys.

items.name: Signer
items.description: apps/signer verifies approval and wallet policy independently. The signing side holds the wallet keys.

items.name: MCP proposal
items.description: The agent proposes a recipient and amount. The server builds an intent, simulates the operation and checks policy for early feedback.

items.name: Request inbox
items.description: The inbox shows the request and links to the confirmation origin. It does not collect the signing approval itself.

items.name: Passkey review
items.description: The signer supplies the operation shown on the separate confirmation page. The person reviews it and the passkey approves the exact operation.

items.name: Signer decision
items.description: The signer binds the assertion to the intent and checks the expected origin, policy, limits and prior use before signing.

items.name: Broadcast worker
items.description: The control plane collects the decision through a durable workflow, requests the signed transaction, broadcasts it and tracks the receipt.

items.name: EVM chain
items.description: A chain receipt lets the control plane report the outcome. Approval, signing and confirmation are different states.

items.name: Workspace owner
items.description: An owner proposes a mandate for one agent and wallet. Approvers authorize the grant through the confirmation page.

items.name: Agent transfer
items.description: The agent still submits each transfer. It does not obtain a signing key or an unrestricted spending allowance.

items.name: Stored mandate
items.description: A grant names the recipient bounds, per-payment, window and total caps, a count limit and an expiry. The signer stores the authoritative grant and can revoke it.

items.name: Signer limits
items.description: The signer checks the live grant and wallet policy against its own counts, then records each use with signing in one transaction.

items.name: Signed transfer
items.description: If the proposal is covered and passes the signer’s checks, it can proceed without a fresh approval. The normal inbox path handles proposals outside the mandate.

items.name: Limit order
items.description: The agent proposes a Hyperliquid order. The control plane checks the venue metadata and the wallet policy for early feedback.

items.name: Order review
items.description: The confirmation page shows the market, side, size, limit price and other order terms before the person approves.

items.name: Venue signing
items.description: The signer validates approval and policy and builds a signed venue request. It is not an EVM transaction.

items.name: Control plane
items.description: The control plane posts the signed request to the venue and follows status by client order ID. A venue can refuse an approved request.

items.name: Hyperliquid
items.description: The venue reports whether the order rests, fills or is refused. The project documents CI tests against fake venues, not a real venue run.

items.name: OS server
items.description: Owns workspace and request records. Some signer state is mirrored here for display, but a mirror does not authorize signing.

items.name: Workflow runtime
items.description: A request can span many steps and wait for a decision. The workflow resumes without depending on a person returning to the inbox.

items.name: Postgres
items.description: Holds control-plane records and workflow state. The repository documents encryption for workflow content and application content, not every database field.

items.name: Signer
items.description: Keeps wallet key access separate from the control plane and applies approvals and limits using signing-side records.

items.name: Signer ledger
items.description: Signer-side SQLite stores authoritative policy and accounting records, including spent limits, approval records and mandate use.

items.name: Person’s browser
items.description: The browser visits the web app and a separate origin for passkey confirmation. This diagram does not name a live host.

items.name: MCP client
items.description: Connects to the MCP entry point. The deployment documents show how to isolate this ingress from the rest of the stack.

items.name: Caddy ingress
items.description: The sample ingress serves the web app and the agent-facing MCP entry point. The confirmation origin remains distinct.

items.name: Server and Postgres
items.description: The control plane coordinates operations. On the split layout this side reaches the separate signer over mutual TLS.

items.name: Confirmation origin
items.description: In the split layout the confirmation service runs on the signing side. It relays confirmation requests to the signer.

items.name: Signer host
items.description: The project documents a single Compose stack and a split-host option. Split hosting can separate the signing side from the control plane.

items.name: apps/web
items.description: Start here for the workspace and approval inbox that a person uses.

items.name: apps/server
items.description: Start here for MCP, request routing, durable workflows and execution.

items.name: apps/signer
items.description: Start here for confirmation records, policy enforcement and signing. apps/approve serves the separate confirmation page.

items.name: packages/protocol
items.description: Shared protocol definitions establish what the control plane and signer exchange.

items.name: packages/world
items.description: The project’s Workflow SDK storage backend. packages/keys contains key management code for encrypted application content.

items.name: deploy/
items.description: Compose, proxy and Kubernetes examples. The deploy README explains which layout each example represents.

items.name: e2e/ and docs/
items.description: Read the architecture and threat model. The end-to-end tests supply evidence for claims about supported behavior. The project is not audited.
